---
title: "What is energy?"
author: "Tim Gorringe"
date: "2023-05-09"
categories: ["Physics"]
format: html
---

In physics an interaction is the action or the influence of one body on another
body. When one billiard ball strikes another billiard ball and their velocities
change, that's an interaction. When cold water's poured in a hot glass and their
temperatures change, that's an interaction. The gravitational force is a
long-range, mutual interaction between masses. The electromagnetic force is a
long-range, mutual interaction between charges.

We can understand many interactions, e.g., collision of billiard balls, by
considering the forces that are exerted and the resulting changes in their
velocities. Through our sense of touch we have a human connection to force. The
notion of forces as pushes and pulls seems real and concrete.

We can't, however, understand the changing temperatures of the cold water in the
hot glass by means of forces. Although the changing temperatures are actually
caused by individual collisions of water / glass molecules, the calculation of
how these forces lead to thermal equilibrium is impossible. However, with energy
it's easy to figure the final temperature of the water and the glass.

The notion of energy is undoubtedly more abstract and subtle than force. The
human feelings of fatigue (low energy) and vitality (high energy) are
psychological experiences that are only loosely related to energy's physical
meaning. So what's this mysterious stuff we call energy?

Hidden beneath the realm of forces and motion are a book keeper and a balance
sheet. Nature's book keeper insures a fundamental quantity in nature's balance
sheet is never changed. The quantity is the energy in the universe. And it
hasn't changed over the 14 billion years since the big bang.

The universe's energy is \`held' in different forms. There's energy associated
with motion that's called kinetic energy. There's energy associated with
gravitational and electrical interactions that's called gravitational and
electrical potential energy. Other classifications of energy include thermal,
chemical and nuclear.

On the grandest scales, galaxies are the owners of the universe's energy through
the motion and the interactions of their parts. Galaxies are giant energy
repositories. On the tiniest scales, subatomic particles are the owners of the
universe's energy their individual motion and their individual interactions.
Think of galaxies as giant energy repositories and subatomic particles are tiny
energy corpuscles.

Although energy is conserved its forms and owners are continually evolving. This
unrest is caused by the interactions between the bodies in the universe. When
forces act they 'do work' which means they transferring energy from one form to
another and / or one owner to another. From the energy perspective the universe
resembles a simmering cauldron of never created, never destroyed, always
churning, energy. We've discovered that within the depths of forces and motion
there's a secluded world of energy.

I want to stress that energy isn't a substance or a material. Energy is a
mathematical quantity. I also want to stress that energy conservation isn't a
mystical commandment. Energy conservation is a mathematical result.

Energy is useful because scientists have uncovered the equations for kinetic,
gravitational, electrical energy. If you sum the energy in all forms for all
bodies it never changes. If you drop a ball from you hand to the floor there's a
decrease in gravitational energy and an increase in kinetic energy. But their
sum is not changed. As planets orbit in elliptical paths around the sun the
kinetic energy is constantly changing and the gravitational energy is constantly
changing. But their sum is not changed.

You might be intrigued why energy is conserved. During the 1700-1800's the
notion that energy is conserved just gradually emerged empirically as different
forms of energy were identified. However, in 1908 the mathematician Emmy Noether
was able to show that conservation of energy arises because the laws of nature
don't change with time. For example, if gravity changed its strength from day to
day then energy isn't conserved. And likewise, if electromagnetism changed its
strength from day to day then energy isn't conserved. So conservation of energy
is actually the echo of a 'natural symmetry' that physical law's don't change
with time.

In physics we implement the notion of energy using potentials. For example, the
gravitational interaction has an associated gravitational potential, and the
electrical interaction has an associated electrical potential. They're potential
are helpful tools for handling the energy transfer when bodies interact with
each other.

The electrical energy PE of a charge q in an electric potential V is given by PE
= q V. Note the resemblance with the electrical force F on a charge in an
electric field E being given by **F** = q **E.** Indeed, like force and energy
are alternative perspective in discussing electrical interactions, the field and
potential are alternative mechanisms for understanding electrical interactions.

As an analogy to E and V picture a contour map of your hometown where contours
represent different elevations, e.g. 900, 1000, 1100 feet. Next imagine adding
arrows to indicate the slope of the terrain at some locations, e.g., your home,
your school. The arrows are the hometown analogy of the electric field and the
contours are the hometown analogy of the electric potential of a charge
arrangement. Positive charges are tops of electric potential mountains, negative
charges are bottoms of electric potential wells, and electric fields are the
downwards slopes of the electric potential landscape. Electrical potentials are
measured in units of Volts.

An important feature of electric potentials and electrical energies is only
electrical potential differences and electrical energy differences are
physically significant. This means that adding everywhere 1.0 Volts to the
electrical potential of a charge distribution has no observable effect. This
means that adding everywhere 1.0 Joules to the electrical energy of a charge
distribution has no observable effect. The actual value of the electric
potential, or the actual value of the electrical energy, is not a measurable,
only differences in potentials or energies are measurable. This is why a
voltmeter has two terminals - it measures differences in electrical potentials
between two points.

So what's it mean to say the electric potential at a distance r from a point
charge q has a value kq/r? It means the potential at distance r from the charge,
and the potential at infinite distance from the charge, are different by kq/r.
It means we've chosen a potential of 0.0 Volts at infinity as our reference for
the electric potential at a distance r from the charge q. In other cases - for
example the electric potential in the region of two oppositely charged plates -
we generally will choice one of the plates to be 0.0 Volts.

Assembling charge distributions involves doing work and storing / harvesting
energy. Imagine assembling an arrangement of two like charges. Because like
charges repel, you'll have to push them together and they'll want to fly apart.
In assembling this arrangement, the electric force will do negative work and the
charge arrangement will store positive electrical energy. You'll do positive
work pushing the charges together. Now imagine assembling an arrangement of two
unlike charges. Because like charges attract, they'll want to fly together and
you'll have to pull them apart. In assembling this arrangement, the electric
force will do positive work and the charge arrangement will store negative
electrical energy. You'll do positive work pulling the charges apart.

The perspective of energy offers an alternative explanation of the stability of
a salt crystal through its binding energy. Consider the aforementioned NaCl
nano-crystal of two positive Na ions and two negative Cl ions. Each ion resides
in the potential of the three remaining ions. Since the unlike charge are closer
and like charge is farther the potential is negative for the positive ions and
positive for the negative ions. Consequently, the electrical energy is negative
for both a Na ion and a Cl ion (i.e., either the charge is positive and
potential is negative or vice versa). The negative electrical energy of each ion
means that removing an ion requires energy.

The calculation isn't so easy for a crystal containing many atoms. You have to
count the number and figure the separation of nearest neighbors, next-nearest,
next-next-nearest neighbors, etc. That's tricky in 3-dimensions. A problem
that's easier is the binding energy on a ion in a one dimensional NaCl crystal.
There are two nearest neighbors at a distance a, two next-nearest neighbors at a
distance 2a, two next-next-nearest neighbors at a distance 3a, etc. Since the
numbers of nth-nearest neighbors is always while the distance of the nth-nearest
neighbors is na, the calculation thus involves a mathematical series
1/1-1/2+1/3-1/4+ ... This a famous series with a sum that is 2 ln 2. Thus the
binding energy is therefore. It's a nice illustration of teamwork between
mathematics and physics.

The understanding that assembling, disassembling and rearranging charges
involves storing / releasing energy is actually a prototype for energy flow in
living things. Foods - carbohydrates, proteins, fats - are rich in
carbon-hydrogen and carbon-oxygen bonds that store electrical energy in electric
charge distributions. We harvest this energy to run our bodies and sustain our
lives.
